subject: Draft Waste Removal Contract RFP
overview: The committee reviewed a draft request for proposals (RFP) for the city's next multi-year waste removal contract. Discussion focused on potential service changes, including a shift to bi-weekly trash collection combined with weekly curbside composting to control rising costs and meet environmental goals.

items.title: Presentation of Draft Waste Removal RFP
items.summary: DPW Commissioner Tim McGivern and Director Alicia Hunt presented a draft RFP for citywide solid waste, recycling, and composting services to replace the expiring contract with Waste Management.

items.title: RFP Scopes and Proposed Service Changes
items.summary: The draft RFP includes options for bi-weekly trash collection paired with weekly composting, a preferred hauler program for businesses and condominiums, and a potential fee for bulky item pickups.

items.title: Committee Discussion and Resident Impact
items.summary: Councilors expressed concerns regarding resident reactions to reduced trash collection frequency, the logistics of composting for seniors and those with limited accessibility, and the removal of certain condominiums from municipal collection.

items.title: Procurement and Fiscal Considerations
items.summary: Officials discussed the $7.5 million current contract cost, the potential for a seven-to-ten-year agreement to lock in rates, and the challenges of insourcing waste services given the lack of city infrastructure.

items.title: Public Participation and Final Disposition
items.summary: A member of the Solid Waste Citizen Task Force thanked city staff for the collaborative process; the matter was kept in committee.
